evidence: statusFor() maps ValidationError/BadRequestError/NotFoundError/ConflictError to HTTP 400/404/409/500. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes is transport work, which belongs in infrastructure.
isJsonParseError() checks for Express body-parser's 'entity.parse.failed' error type, which is framework-specific logic.
errorHandler (ErrorRequestHandler) writes res.status().json() responses and logs with console.error. This is HTTP adapter work.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This is an Express error-handling middleware in the infrastructure layer. Everything it does is transport work. It turns domain and request errors into HTTP status codes (400, 404 or 409, with 500 as the fallback). It spots body-parser JSON parse failures, logs unexpected errors, and writes JSON error responses. Turning errors into status codes is HTTP adapter work, not a business rule. The file contains no domain logic, persistence or application orchestration.
